objetivos.necesitas: You need to "see" beneath the clouds and measure gravity: microwave radiometer, gravity science, magnetometer.
Cameras and instruments that measure heat and composition: infrared, radiometer, ultraviolet.
Particle and field detectors: magnetometer, particles, plasma waves.

por_que.energia: At Jupiter, sunlight is 25 times weaker. Juno compensated with 3 solar arrays totaling ~60 m²: 14 kW at Earth drops to about 400 W out there.
por_que.antena: Ka-band is not for faster data: it enables ultra-precise gravity measurements, the key to discovering whether Jupiter has a solid core.
por_que.blindaje: The titanium radiation vault (~200 kg, ~1 cm thick per side) shields electronics from the harshest radiation in the solar system.
por_que.propulsion: About 2,000 kg of propellant: more than half the spacecraft's mass. The orbital insertion burn lasted 35 minutes.
por_que.cohete: Atlas V 551, the most powerful version of the Atlas V, with 5 solid boosters.
por_que.orbita: In 2016, two helium valves malfunctioned. NASA decided not to risk the engine burn and remained in the 53-day orbit.
por_que.final: At mission end, Juno will plunge into Jupiter to avoid contaminating Europa, which could harbor life.

briefing: Mission question: How did Jupiter form, and does it have a solid core?
You will primarily investigate the planet's INTERIOR: choose sensors that peer beneath the clouds and measure gravity.
You have 1,250 million dollars, a destination 5.2 AU away, and the most brutal radiation in the solar system waiting for you.

eventos.texto: The spacecraft separated from the rocket. It is tumbling uncontrollably and the battery is draining. Deploy the solar arrays now?

opciones.resultado: Successful deployment. The solar cells have started charging.
Safer, but the battery level dropped significantly while waiting.

eventos.texto: We need to fire the engine to steer back toward Earth for a gravity assist slingshot. How much delta-v do we apply?
eventos.resultado_mal: We will have to correct later: extra propellant wasted.

eventos.texto: We flew within 560 km of Earth and gained free speed! But the spacecraft tripped into safe mode (just like the real Juno did). Reboot the systems in sequence.

exito.resultado: Systems recovered. Earth's gravity assist boosted our speed without spending any fuel.

fallo.resultado: Recovery took days and the electronics suffered damage.

eventos.texto: A coronal mass ejection is heading right for us. Shut down sensitive instruments before it strikes.
An attitude maneuver misaligned the antenna: Earth can no longer hear us. From the cockpit, point the antenna until you reacquire the signal.

exito.resultado: Signal reacquired. Ground control breathes a sigh of relief: each message takes about 40 minutes to arrive, even at light speed.

fallo.resultado: Without contact, the spacecraft autonomously entered safe mode until mission control re-established contact.

eventos.texto: Sunlight is 25 times weaker out here. Check the console: if the power balance is negative, shut down anything you don't need until arrival.
Already in the 53-day orbit, two helium check valves take minutes to open instead of seconds. The original plan was to fire the engine to trim down to a 14-day orbit.

opciones.texto: Risk the engine burn (more orbits, more science)
opciones.resultado_ok: It worked! Shorter orbits and more perijove science passes.
opciones.resultado_mal: The engine cut off mid-burn: entered safe mode and suffered subsystem damage.

opciones.resultado: Fewer perijove passes, but the spacecraft is safe. That is what NASA decided in 2017.

pregunta: How did Jupiter form, and does it have a solid core?
crucero_texto: The cruise lasts 5 years. We will wake you whenever a situation requires your decision.
llegada_texto: We are arriving at over 200,000 km/h. The real Juno fired its engine for 35 minutes to brake.

pistas.cohete: Juno is heavy: the rocket must lift all that mass toward Jupiter… without breaking the budget.
pistas.propulsion: You need 2,000 m/s of delta-v. Watch the gauge as you hover over components.
pistas.energia: Jupiter is 5 times farther from the Sun than Earth: sunlight is 25 times weaker.
pistas.antena: The signal weakens with distance. Does any instrument require a special antenna?
pistas.blindaje: Jupiter harbors the most intense radiation belts in the solar system.
pistas.instrumentos: Cover all 3 objectives (the interior is worth half). Be careful not to generate more data than you can transmit.

final_texto: You deorbited the spacecraft into Jupiter to protect Europa: just like NASA's plan.

orbitas.descripcion: A very stretched polar orbit: Juno swings close to Jupiter once every 53 days.
orbitas.por_que: This has been Juno's real orbit since 2016, after a problem with its helium valves. There are fewer close passes, but the radiation dose is spread out and the probe lasts longer.

orbitas.descripcion: The polar orbit planned at the start: one close pass every 14 days.
orbitas.por_que: It makes about 4 times more close passes, so more science, but each year it soaks up much more radiation and it needs an extra burn that uses delta-v.

orbitas.descripcion: An orbit above the planet's equator, never crossing the poles.
orbitas.por_que: It avoids the worst of the radiation belts, so the probe lasts longer, but it barely sees the auroras and the poles, which are the most interesting part of Juno.
